guides.summary: Survey the Python workflow, C++ runtime boundary, backend status, research labs, installation paths, and documentation map.
Install Riftco Transformer, verify native tensor math, build the C++ runtime, and run a short Python training smoke test.
Assemble a small decoder-only transformer and trace one complete forward, backward, and Adam update.
Understand contiguous storage, shapes, strides, scalar tensors, indexing, reshape, and backend transfer.
Learn the checked tensor-operation contracts, broadcasting rules, reductions, and relationship to autograd.
Follow reverse-mode automatic differentiation from graph construction through gradient accumulation and custom gradients.
Understand embeddings, linear layers, normalization, activations, feed-forward composition, softmax, and cross-entropy.
Trace causal multi-head self-attention shapes, masking, materialized execution, and exact memory-linear execution.
Follow embeddings, pre-normalized residual blocks, final normalization, and the language-model head through a decoder-only transformer.
Understand how Python orchestrates seeded batches and metrics while C++ executes fresh graphs, all-position or time-range cross-entropy, backward, and Adam.
Compose Python-owned pretraining and post-training with immutable artifact handoff and native-backed local serving.
Attach low-rank adapters, optimize only adapter parameters, compare ranks without test leakage, and merge for serving.
Fine-tune LoRA adapters over an NF4-packed frozen base while preserving packed storage during computation.
Run incremental generation with per-request decoder state, paged KV storage, and the local C or Python serving surfaces.
Trade replay computation for lower retained autograd state at transformer-block boundaries.
Capture, validate, and restore exact FP32 full-training or LoRA Adam state, RNG state, and built-in batch-source position.
Convert Riftco models through strict SafeTensors, Hugging Face-style, GGUF v3, and ONNX boundaries without hiding architecture incompatibility.
Run the Linux fake-PJRT source gate or the non-skippable real Cloud TPU hardware acceptance preset and record reproducible evidence.
Diagnose configuration, build, backend, shape, training, artifact, Python loading, and documentation failures.
Map Python orchestration and the C++ runtime from model/autograd through compiler, lowering, generic programmed composition, serving, and backends.
Understand parameter registration, ownership, recursive names, nonmoving modules, and transactional backend transfer.
Understand byte and byte-pair tokenization strategies, token IDs, UTF-8 boundaries, and shifted next-token windows.
Understand bias-corrected Adam, global gradient clipping, contiguous or bounded-page state, and transactional updates.
Look up C++ APIs, ABI 2.8 model and optimizer surfaces, checkpoints, and model interchange.
Look up CMake backends plus model, program branch, lowering, intervention, training, post-training, and serving configuration contracts.
Look up Python training, conditional-reversal quick/paper labs, data preparation, fine-tuning, and serving commands and evidence boundaries.
Find concise definitions for tensor, model, training, backend, quantization, serving, compiler, and analysis terms.
Use the native dense Llama/Mistral topology and understand its strict config, sliding-window, tokenizer, checkpoint, and binding boundaries.
Understand ProgramAugmentedModel ownership, ABI/Python composition, repository-lab policy, dependency direction, and extension seams.
Inspect backend selection, adapter contracts, ABI 2.8 model/state handles, accelerator scope, and the dependency-free Python client.
Follow Cajal, sparse map import, neural lowering, public ProgramAugmentedModel composition, and the Python-owned F/P/T/I evidence boundary.

Trace Quang T. Nguyen's neuro-symbolic research direction from typed program compilation and neural lowering to transformer experiments, causal interpretation, and DreamCoder-inspired program learning.
Prepare audited Hugging Face data and run controlled TinyStories, Dolly, LoRA-rank, and fine-tuning comparisons.
Measure train, validation, and held-out test behavior without using the test split for model or rank selection.
Track the completed generic programmed/ABI/Python slice, active evidence milestones, acceptance checks, and deferred work.
Place changes at the right ownership boundary, add evidence-driven tests, validate proportionately, and prepare an honest handoff.
Author professional tutorials, how-to guides, concepts, references, explanations, and source-grounded experiment reports.
